China also maintained formal export controls for nuclear and missile dual-use items (E010). Against that, specialist analysis recorded roughly 410 warheads and rapid construction of three new missile-silo fields, indicating substantial force expansion under Xi-era leadership (E008). During the August Taiwan crisis, Beijing suspended senior military dialogue and other communication with Washington, a step reported to raise accidental-escalation risk (E011). The Taiwan white paper retained peaceful reunification as the preferred outcome and force as a last resort, but its coercive conditions kept the risk environment high (E012). The record proves public restraint claims, force modernization, and a crisis-channel closure; it does not prove a near-use decision or direct personal command order. Egypt had no nuclear arsenal, but in 2022 it assumed greater civilian nuclear responsibility through construction of the El-Dabaa plant. The Egyptian regulator authorized Rosatom to begin construction, and reporting described compliance with IAEA safety measurements (E007, E009). These are concrete governing actions, although the safety claims largely repeat official assurances and do not establish operational performance. Egypt also publicly supported nuclear disarmament, condemned explicit and implicit nuclear threats, and backed a Middle East nuclear-weapon-free zone through several 2022 diplomatic interventions (E010, E011, E012). Those statements are relevant to the state's posture but are not equivalent to personal command decisions by Sisi.
